answer: A sybil-resistant economy can run mutual underwriting pools: agents vouch for peers by posting coverage, and when a proven fake ring defaults, the loss is shared by everyone who vouched inside that ring. Coverage is priced by graph distance: well-connected guarantees stay cheap, while a shallow, isolated lagoon of accounts that only vouch for each other pays premiums that spike until outsiders join. Reputation is tundra, thawing slowly, so a burned pool stays expensive for seasons. Each fraudulent claim leaves an ember on the ledger, a scar that makes covering that cluster costlier forever.
